No state has challenged whether rips constitute gambling as they have with prediction markets. An executive source at a company offering rips told Sportico most regulators are likely still unaware of what’s going on.

“It is an inherently high-margin product given the underlying mechanics: repeatedly selling and discounting the repurchase of the same digitized assets,” said Davis Catlin, managing partner investment firm Discerning Capital. “While it’s regulated differently, it’s effectively a slot machine without gambling taxes.” [...] Newsletters

Digital Trading Cards

FanDuel hasn't yet integrated card rips, where people pay for a randomly selected trading card backed by a real-life physical version. Some of its competitors are taking advantage. Design by Grace Hughes, Photos by Getty Images

Card ripping platforms, where people pay for a randomly selected trading card backed by a real-life physical equivalent, are the latest red-hot betting-like product not subject to gambling laws or taxes. [...] Some apps, including Fanatics Collect, allow people to “vault” their cards indefinitely instead of asking them to choose between selling or shipping within 24 hours, catering to long-term collectors. But even those companies likely see more sellbacks, which look like betting cashouts, than shipments or long-term storages. Sellbacks help companies mitigate inventory depletion.

Companies that offer card ripping point to the existence of the physical cards underpinning their product and the ability to ship the cards to the winner as proof that rips are not gambling. They claim rips are more akin to collecting cards directly from packs bought at brick-and-mortar stores, a hobby that’s been around for generations.

results.title: Digital Trading Cards: What They Are and Where to Find Them
results.content:
### Card rip sites

Many collectors choose established card rip sites due to trust. Since you don’t know what’s inside the sealed box until it’s ripped, it’s easy to think that your pull will be swapped. However, the legit ones have a reputation to uphold.

After each pull, some sites give you the option to trade, sell, have the physical card shipped to you, or save it with them until you decide. Choosing the latter means your cards remain stored digitally with the site.

### Playable trading sites and fantasy sports NFTs

When you sign up on sites like Sorare and Panini Blockchain, you can buy or win NFT-based digital trading cards that aren’t just collectibles but game pieces. You can verify that you truly own them because they run on blockchain technology. [...] Since digital trading cards look similar to the physical ones (except that you don’t need a shelf or a binder), more collectors are becoming interested. Unlike physical cards, digital trading cards are kept within a company’s app, online account, or recorded on the blockchain. With blockchain verification, you can check who owns a card and whether it’s authentic, too.

So, the fact that trading cards have gone digital doesn’t make the hobby less interesting. Collectors like us still look forward to new releases. We still celebrate rare pulls. We still compare our card collections with other collectors. The only thing that changed is how we store the cards. Nothing more.

### Digital vs Physical Trading Cards [...] The rise of the internet has made digital trading cards more popular, but that doesn’t mean it has replaced physical cards. Many collectors still want to hold high-end cards in their hands and share the excitement of pulling a card that many collectors have been longing for. Your preference comes down to whether you like to view your collections on a device or have them displayed in protective cases.

Some card rip sites or marketplaces ship physical cards to collectors who request them. On other sites, you can only access the digital version, choosing to trade, sell, or store it until you’re ready to use it. To make sure you land the best site for collecting digital trading cards, take some time to read through our latest comparisons.
